new_statements.translation: It should be noted that (except in Galela and Ternate) almost all words take the stress on the 3rd syllable from the end. Where this is not the case an accent mark (') is given. [...] The ' in Waioli breaks the liaison between two syllables; e.g. tu'angere 'eight' is pronounced as if it were written tu angere.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Default word stress on the antepenultimate syllable in Waioli (as in Tabaru, Ibu and Loda; Galela and Ternate excepted); words deviating from this carry a written acute in Fortgens' lists, and the marked Waioli exceptions are penultimate (kaúna 'dog', tubaíe 'youth', romodídi 'two', roánge 'three', romotóo 'five', tumudíngi 'seven'). Since Waioli, like Tabaru, has added echo vowels to old final consonants (ngo'omo 'road', odu'u), the surface antepenult often equals the historical penult (cf. Fortgens 1928 on Tabaru).
new_statements.exceptions: Deviations from antepenult are marked individually with an acute in the word lists (in the Waioli column mostly penultimate stress, incl. several numerals and kaúna, tubaíe); no rule for the exceptions is given. Disyllables are not discussed (antepenult impossible; unmarked disyllables like banjo 'water', oti 'canoe' presumably penult/initial).
new_statements.domain_note: Citation forms in elicited comparative word lists (missionary fieldwork at Tobae with Waioli-speaking women married to Tabaru men, 1904); the remark is a blanket statement over the Tabaru, Waioli, Ibu and Loda columns, not a Waioli-specific phonology. Modern second-hand coding of the closest described variety, Sahu/Pa'disua (Visser & Voorhoeve 1987:19 via StressTyp2 and WALS 14A), is likewise 'antepenultimate, fixed' with irregular exceptions; Severn 1995 calls Sahu stress non-contrastive with rules undetermined, Pikkert & Pikkert 1995 call it phonemic citing V&V 1987:19.
new_statements.identity_note: Fortgens' 'Waioli'sch' is the Waioli of the NW Halmahera west coast north of Jailolo (Suüru/Dóusu area) = Glottolog waio1238; his stress remark is a blanket statement over his Tabaru (taba1263), Waioli, Ibu (ibuu1240) and Loda (lolo1264) lists. Visser & Voorhoeve 1987, Voorhoeve 1988 and Severn 1995 treat Waioli as a dialect of Sahu (sahu1245); the StressTyp2 and WALS 'antepenultimate' codings are for the Sahu Pa'disua lect (padi1242), second-hand from V&V 1987, not for Waioli itself.

sources.note: p. 33, introducing the Tabaru/Waioli/Ibu/Galela/Loda comparative lists: except in Galela and Ternate, almost all words take the stress on the third syllable from the end; where not, an accent is written. Waioli forms with marked deviations in the lists pp. 33-45 include kaúna 'dog', tubaíe 'youth', romodídi '2', roánge '3', romotóo '5', tumudíngi '7' (penult); unmarked e.g. tu'angere '8', siworo '9', mosolese, sengene (antepenult).

sources.citation: Severn, John A. 1995. The phonemic syllable in Sahu: a computer-aided phonological analysis. NUSA 38: 71-87.
sources.note: Sahu (Pa'disua), not Waioli: sec. 5.1 pp. 82-83 'The stress rules have not been fully determined yet... it seems safe to assume that stress is non-contrastive and therefore non-phonemic'; sec. 5.2 stress in vocoid clusters falls on the syllable with the consonant onset; loans keep source stress.

sources.citation: StressTyp2 database, language 658 'Sahu', lect 747 'Pa'disua; Palisua' (Goedemans, van der Hulst et al.), source Visser & Voorhoeve 1987.
sources.note: Second-hand for Sahu: primary stress pattern A / 3R 'the antepenultimate syllable', plus an 'A (IRR)' exceptional pattern; affix comment ['demo] 'word', [de'demo] 'darling'; sole source Visser & Voorhoeve 1987.

sources.citation: WALS Online (Goedemans & van der Hulst), features 14A/15A/16A for Sahu (sah), source Visser-and-Voorhoeve-1987.
sources.note: Second-hand for Sahu: 14A = Antepenultimate fixed stress; 15A = Fixed stress (no weight-sensitivity); 16A = No weight.

sources.note: Waioli data taken from Fortgens 1905 (p. 371). p. 409: the languages of the group differ audibly in where they lay the stress (Galela never shifts stress with suffixes, Tobelo shifts it onto the suffix, Madole stresses the enclitic exponents); nothing specific to Waioli.
